questions.stemHtml: Which virus causes antigenic shift?
questions.solutionHtml:
Influenza

The picture shows segmented RNA virus

Antigenic shift:

  • Abrupt, drastic and discontinuous variation resulting in a novel virus
  • New surface antigen not related to previous
  • Due to genetic reassortment between 2 strains, presumably during coinfection of a single host
  • Causes major epidemics and pandemic


Jawetz, Melnick, & Adelberg’s Medical microbiology - 28th edition - page 420

questions.stemHtml: Identify the egg in the image:
questions.solutionHtml:
Hymenolepis nana
  • The given image of the egg and lifecycle is that of Hymenolepis nana.
  • nana egg is colourless, almost transparent, oval, 30–50 µm (micrometres) in diameter, and has polar filaments.
  • When shed in stool they are immediately infective and survive up to 10 days in the external environment, they are embryonated and have 6-hooked oncospheres inside the shells.
  • Shell consists of two distinct membranes.
  • On the inner membrane there are two small “knobs” or poles from which 4–8 filaments arise and spread out between the two membranes.


Paniker’s Textbook of Medical Parasitology - 8th edition - page 155, 156

questions.stemHtml: A forest worker developed macules over his forearm, which later became nodules. On histology the following image is seen. Choose the correct statement about the given causative organism?

options.label: B
options.text: Infection can spread and involve underlying tissue, tendon, muscle or joints

options.label: C
options.text: Angioinvasion is common especially in people with hemolytic anaemia

options.label: D
options.text: These bodies are formed by engulfment of the dead fungi by macrophages

questions.solutionHtml:
It is a dematiaceous fungi
  • The given image shows copper penny bodies. This along with the clinical presentation is suggestive of chromoblastomycosis. It is a dematiaceous fungus.
  • Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic granulomatous infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue caused by several different dematiaceous fungi (brown pigment-producing), resulting in the formation of slow-growing, warty plaques, cauliflower-like lesions which may ulcerate. The disease generally remains localised, but lymphatic spread may occur



Ananthanarayanan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology - 7th edition - page 605-611

questions.stem: A patient presents lesions on the black eschar on the back with chills and high grade fever. The probable cause could be?
questions.solutionHtml:
Scrub Typhus
  • Option A is the correct answer
  • Scrub typhus, also known as bush typhus, is a disease caused by a bacteria called Orientia tsutsugamushi. Scrub typhus is spread to people through bites of infected chiggers (larval mites). The most common symptoms of scrub typhus include fever, headache, body aches, and sometimes rash. Black eschar is present at the site where larvae bites. 

DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF AN ESCHAR




Ananthanarayanan and Paniker’s Textbook of Microbiology - 10th edition - page 415

questions.stemHtml: Match the following disease/organism with stains used to demonstrate them: (MICRO) Choose the correct answer from below given code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1-d, 2-a, 3-b, 4-c
  • Fite-Faraco stain:  Routinely used method to demonstrate Mycobacterium leprae in tissue sections. FF staining is more sensitive than ZN method in detection of Mycobacterium leprae
  • Giemsa staining: It is used for the detection of malarial parasite
  • ZN staining: a rapid and practical method for detecting acid-fast bacilli (AFB), especially in low-income countries, due to its rapidity, low cost, and high positive predictive value for tuberculosis and leprosy
  • Actinomyces : Gram-positive filamentous bacilli. They havre branching, filamentous morphology


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page 398

questions.stem: Fungus having non-septate hyphae and producing sporangiospores is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Phycomycetes
  • Phycomycetes are lower fungi which have non-septate hyphae and form endogenous asexual spores (sporangiospores) contained within sporangia
  • Systematic classification of fungi, based on their sexual spore formation, recognizes 4 classes:
  • Phycomycetes: Non-septate hyphae, produces sporangiospores (asexual spores), oospores and zygospores (sexual spores)
  • Ascomycetes: Septate hyphae, Produces conidia (asexual spores) and ascospores (sexual spores)
  • Basidiomycetes: Septate hyphae, Produces conidia (asexual spores) and basidiospores (sexual spores)
  • Fungi imperfecti: Septate hyphae, Produces conidia (asexual spores) and sexual phase has not been identified.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page 912

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presented with diarrhoea and blood. On investigation of stool samples, the organism was Gram negative non lactose fermenter, and non-motile, oxidase negative, H2S negative. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Shigella
  • The given scenario is a case of Shigella dysentery
  • Inability to ferment lactose is used to differentiate Salmonella and Shigella from E.coli. Salmonella is usually motile and produces H2S with few exceptions.

Shigella

  • Gram negative bacilli.
  • Non - motile
  • Facultatively anaerobic
  • Non-spore-forming rod
  • Mannitol Fermentation Based Classification used


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 275

questions.stemHtml: A boy presented with fever, chills, myalgias, weakness, nausea, vomiting, cough. headache, and malaise following a forest safari. identify the following causative organism from the given image:
questions.solutionHtml:
Anaplasma phagocytophilum
  • The given image shows a morula in a granulocyte which is seen in anaplasma. Please note that the patient does not have any rash.
  • Anaplasma phagocytophilum is an obligate gram-negative, intracellular bacterium that causes an acute febrile illness known as anaplasmosis or human granulocytic anaplasmosis (HGA)
    • Rash is uncommon in anaplasmosis. Some patients infected with E. chaffeensis develop a maculopapular or petechial rash on the trunk and extremities.
  • Ehrlichia chaffeensis is a gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterium that is transmitted by hard ticks
  • Clinical presentation of Ehrlichia chaffeensis infection is similar to that of Anaplasma infection.
  • Severe human monocytic ehrlichiosis is characterised by meningoencephalitis, renal failure, respiratory failure, and shock.
  • The treatment of choice for human monocytic ehrlichiosis is
  • Rickettsia rickettsii causes rocky mountain spotted fever and is transmitted by ticks.
  • Rickettsia conorii causes Mediterranean spotted fever and is transmitted by infected ticks and mites.


Jawetz, Melnick, & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology - 28th edition - page 359-362
